examGuide.title: Approach the exam question
examGuide.body: For modular additive groups, an element a is self-inverse when 2a≡0 mod n; its order is n/gcd(a,n). In a direct product, equations hold componentwise and an element’s order is the lcm of component orders. Lagrange’s theorem constrains subgroup orders but does not assert that every divisor is the order of a subgroup in an arbitrary group.

examGuide.title: Worked problem
examGuide.body:
What is the order of (2,3) in the additive group Z6×Z8?

**Answer: 24.** The order of 2 in Z6 is 6/gcd(2,6)=3. The order of 3 in Z8 is 8/gcd(3,8)=8. The tuple returns to zero after lcm(3,8)=24 additions.

examGuide.title: Conditions and edge cases
examGuide.body:
The identity in an additive group is zero. The inverse of a mod n is −a mod n, not generally its multiplicative inverse.

Integers modulo n under multiplication are not generally a group; restrict to units to obtain inverses.
